The College is focused on teaching and learning, and emphasizes student success at all levels and is interested in candidates who value those same attributes. Candidates must appreciate and understand the mission and purpose of an open-access, community and technical college. As a collaborative, energetic leader, the successful candidate will demonstrate excellent interpersonal and communication skills; a strong commitment to student success; comfortable with change, innovation, and technology; and the use of data for decision-making.The Director will report directly to the Dean of Math and Science and have a voice in the MLT program decisions. The MLT Director is responsible for coordinating the delivery of instruction, for ensuring the quality of instruction, budget management, and for the overall leadership, organization, administration, supervision, and effectiveness of the program. The director is responsible for operating the MLT program in accordance with NAACLS Standards and maintaining program accreditation. The Director will oversee continuous quality improvement activities, supervise program faculty and staff, maintain regular communication with students, faculty, clinical affiliates, administration, and program personnel, and ensure the quality and effectiveness of both didactic and clinical education experiences. The Director is a faculty member who will teach the equivalent of 15 credit hours per semester.ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Oversee all aspects of the MLT program; maintain compliance with all NAACLS accreditation standards; coordinate accreditation activities, reports, and self-studies; and ensure the overall effectiveness of the program. Participate in the preparation, development, and management of the program budget, including identifying resources to meet program needs. Oversee the MLT course schedule in collaboration with the Director of Allied Health to promote student engagement, persistence, and retention. Periodically evaluate the course schedule, curriculum, student learning outcomes, program outcomes, and all aspects of the MLT program through a continuous quality improvement process. Use assessment data, graduate outcomes, employer feedback, advisory committee recommendations, certification examination performance, retention, placement, and graduation rates to improve program effectiveness and student success.
